## Natural history notes

A medium-sized owlet moth characterized by mottled brown to grayish-brown forewings with darker patches, pale lines, and a sturdy body typical of armyworm moths. In Florida, it is found in gardens, farms, fields, roadsides, wetlands, parks, and other open or disturbed habitats where sweet potato and other low herbaceous host plants occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on leaves of sweet potato and related plants, sometimes acting as crop pests and helping move herbaceous plant growth into the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
